title: The Aquarium Closes at Midnight
genre: indie pop with subtle R&B inflections
theme: Healing begins when you stop waiting for someone to return and learn to make a life that glows on its own.
story: A night-shift aquarium cleaner keeps finding small reminders of an ex in the closed blue galleries: a forgotten hair tie, a name scratched into a bench, a voicemail saved but never played. On the evening the ex is due to collect their last box, the narrator prepares the apartment like a museum of their relationship. The ex cancels by text, and instead of collapsing, the narrator walks back to the aquarium and releases a rescued moon jelly into the main tank. By sunrise, the empty apartment feels less like abandonment and more like a room finally available for something new.
setting: A public aquarium after closing, in late autumn; blue tank light spills across wet tile, filtration pumps hum under the floor, and dawn rain beads on the staff entrance.
perspective: First person, present tense, a night-shift aquarium cleaner speaking directly to the absent ex.
motifs: a hair tie on a bench
style_prompt: Indie pop with subtle R&B inflections, 104 BPM, tender and nocturnal with a quietly triumphant lift. Intimate clear lead vocal with restrained ache, electric piano, muted guitar, warm synth bass, crisp drum kit, and glassy mallet tones. Build from close-room minimalism into a luminous final chorus. Polished production with wet, reflective textures.
